For AuditLogEntry.datetime this means math.floor receives a datetime and cursor values are not converted back to datetimes, so the first non-empty optimized request or any non-zero cursor will raise TypeError or a database type error."

Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises an exception instead of paginating efficiently. Because cursor offsets are client-supplied, this can cause 500 errors for any admin using or being sent a crafted cursor."

If a cursor contains a negative offset, the paginator will slice the QuerySet with a negative start index. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing, so a malformed or malicious cursor with is_prev true can cause an unhandled exception on any endpoint using a BasePaginator subclass."

findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot paginate datetime-ordered audit logs
findings.body: The endpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator while ordering by -datetime. OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key), and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value. For AuditLogEntry.datetime this means math.floor receives a datetime and cursor values are not converted back to datetimes, so the first non-empty optimized request or any non-zero cursor will raise TypeError or a database type error.

findings.title: Optimized paginator uses unsupported negative QuerySet slicing
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, OptimizedCursorPaginator allows start_offset to remain negative and then slices the Django QuerySet with that offset. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so this raises an exception instead of paginating efficiently. Because cursor offsets are client-supplied, this can cause 500 errors for any admin using or being sent a crafted cursor.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets to QuerySet slicing for previous pages
findings.body: The change sets start_offset directly to cursor.offset when cursor.is_prev is true. If a cursor contains a negative offset, the paginator will slice the QuerySet with a negative start index. Django QuerySets reject negative indexing, so a malformed or malicious cursor with is_prev true can cause an unhandled exception on any endpoint using a BasePaginator subclass.

findings.title: Cursor offsets are accepted as negative without validation
findings.body: Cursor.__init__ converts offset with int(offset) and the added comment explicitly permits negative offsets, but there is no validation or paginator-level contract for this behavior. Existing cursor pagination logic generally assumes offsets are non-negative, and negative offsets can propagate into QuerySet slicing or cursor arithmetic. If negative offsets are intended, they need explicit validation and safe paginator support; otherwise they should be rejected or clamped.

findings.title: Ordering reversal is lost due to assignment to order_b instead of order_by
findings.body: In BasePaginator.build_queryset, when converting an existing descending order to ascending, the code assigns the new ordering tuple to queryset.query.order_b rather than queryset.query.order_by. The ordering change is silently discarded, so backward pagination may continue to use the wrong sort direction and return incorrect or inconsistent pages.

findings.title: No tests cover the new optimized pagination behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces a query-parameter-controlled paginator switch, an admin-only advanced mode, negative-offset handling, and a new OptimizedCursorPaginator, but no tests are included for these paths. Tests should verify datetime cursor compatibility, safe handling or rejection of negative offsets, and that the optimized path is only used by authorized users.
